So claim 1 is true, which requires at least one of claims 4 and 5 to be false. Hence (t4, t5) ≠ (T, T).

The pairs with exactly one consistent assignment are (1,3), (1,5), (2,3), (2,5), (3,1), (3,2), (3,4), (4,1), (4,2), (5,3), (5,4), which is 11 pairs.

**Counting labelings.** Once Diophantus and Euclid are placed, the other three people fill the remaining three claims in 3! = 6 ways. The claims' content does not depend on who said them, so the truth analysis is unaffected. The total is 11 × 6 = 66.
